input.quote: At the request of Harpoon, AbbVie shall permit an independent public accounting firm of nationally recognized standing designated by Harpoon and reasonably acceptable to AbbVie, [***], to audit the books and records maintained pursuant to this Section 6.11 to ensure the accuracy of all reports and payments made hereunder, including any permitted deductions from Net Sales pursuant to Section 1.108. Such examinations may not (a) be conducted for any [***] [***] (b) be conducted more than once in any [***] period or (c) be [***] (unless a previous audit revealed an underpayment with respect to such [***]).
input.rationale: Section 6.11 is the only audit right binding us (AbbVie); the inspection rights in Article 3 run in our favour against Harpoon. On its material terms 6.11 meets the preferred position: scope is limited to books and records supporting Net Sales/royalty reporting (no access to our systems, no unannounced or unlimited audits, and the auditor may report only whether reports are correct plus specific discrepancies); it may be conducted no more than once in any stated period; it must be performed by an independent nationally recognized accounting firm reasonably acceptable to us; and Harpoon bears the cost unless the audit reveals a variance above the stated threshold. Section 6.13 requires the auditor/Audit Expert to sign a confidentiality agreement with AbbVie, and 6.12 provides a neutral dispute mechanic. The frequency period, notice period and variance percentage are redacted ([***]) and should be confirmed as 12 months / 30 days' notice / 5% (fallback 15 days / 10%), but the clause architecture is compliant and nothing falls into walk-away territory, so no redline is warranted.
